title: Acyclicity of C_d(Φ, V)[φ_x] for vertices x
body_html:
Acyclicity of $C_\bullet(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$

Lemma. Assume (T3), (T4) (for the support lemma) and (K3) (for the contraction extension). For each vertex $x \in A$, the chain complex $C_\bullet(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$ (augmented by $\epsilon_V|_{V[\phi_x]} : C_0[\phi_x] \to V[\phi_x]$) is acyclic.

Hypothesis tightness. Direct uses: (T3), (T4) (via the support lemma), (K3) (via the contraction extension). (T1), (T2), (T5), (S) play no role in this acyclicity proof.
proof_html:
By [[node:coefficient_systems.support_in_BSx]], every element of $C_d(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$ is supported in $\BSigma_x = K_x \cdot A$. By Contraction c on C_d(Φ, V)[φ_x], the contraction $c$ of $C_\bullet(A)$ to the vertex $x$ extends $G$-equivariantly to $C_\bullet(\BSigma_x)$ and preserves the $\phi_x$-isotypic subcomplex: $$c \colon C_d(\Phi, V)[\phi_x] \;\longrightarrow\; C_{d+1}(\Phi, V)[\phi_x].$$

The contraction satisfies the homotopy identity $$\partial \circ c + c \circ \partial = \mathrm{id} - i \circ p,$$ where $i \circ p$ is the projection-then-inclusion to the constant 0-cycle at $x$ (i.e.\ the chain $x \otimes \epsilon$ in degree 0, zero in positive degrees). Hence:

  • In positive degrees $d \ge 1$, $i \circ p = 0$, so $\partial c + c \partial = \mathrm{id}$, which gives exactness: every cycle $z$ with $\partial z = 0$ satisfies $z = \partial(cz)$.

  • In degree 0, $\partial c(z) = z - i(p(z))$, so $z$ and $i(p(z))$ are in the same equivalence class modulo boundaries; $i(p(z)) = x \otimes p(z)$ with $p(z) \in V[\phi_x]$, so $\epsilon_V(z) = p(z)$ surjects onto $V[\phi_x]$.

Combining: the augmented complex $C_\bullet(\Phi, V)[\phi_x] \to V[\phi_x] \to 0$ is exact. $\square$

This is the per-vertex acyclicity feeding into the global resolution theorem Resolution theorem: C_•(Φ, V) → V (Thm 7.1.7) once $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ is assumed to be a Serre subcategory.
